themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say model drift and personalization swamp any effect they cause, and the same missing answer key drives the work on incrementality measurement, identity resolution, content review, and B2B buying-group signal.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every answer on safe agent execution builds a proxy or gateway with spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spends have no rollback, and the consent enforcement answers put a single checkpoint in front of all data leaving the warehouse.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, a message, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, trained model, or private chat that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The consent and deletion answers call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from trained models, and the B2B signal answers say early buying talk now happens in private channels that cannot be observed at all.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models agree agents profit by pretending to be human and propose perks for honest disclosure, while the journey orchestration and semantic context layer answers call the blocker channel budgets and departmental politics rather than technology.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three build an approved-claims library and limit what can be said, because deciding whether wording makes a supported claim is a judgment expert reviewers themselves dispute, and the semantic layer answers say one definition of customer is the wrong target.
